description.value: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover fMRI study investigated acute nicotine effects on food-cue reactivity and hypothalamic functional coupling in healthy never-smokers under fasting and post-glucose conditions.

spans.text: Thus, we investigated 26 normal-weighted never-smokers who received either nicotine (2 mg) or placebo gums following a double-blinded randomized cross-over design.

value: we hypothesized that nicotine alters (a) processing of food pictures in the hypothalamus and (b) functional coupling of this cluster to the NAcc.

value: During nicotine sessions, the OGTT reduced functional coupling in a more superior network involving primary and secondary taste-processing regions, top-down visual processing, selection and initiation, motor execution, and inhibition of actions.

During nicotine sessions, the homeostatic feedback mechanism of the hypothalamic cluster is decoupled from the hedonic-hunger network, as reflected by attenuated food-cue reactivity and reduced functional coupling with the nucleus accumbens during food-picture blocks.
